items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: He was a fine drummer, this guy, Black Benny, was a fine drummer.

ctx.x: I never knew him, but I heard a lot of guys talk about him.

Well, he was a summons on him, Red Happy. He used to, he was with John Robichaud. Oh man. He was a fine drummer, this guy, Black Benny, was a fine drummer. He got killed, a poison or something. I think he got killed. He had some nice trumpet players around here like Buddy Petit, Ricka, Rene, Chris Kelly, Lee Collins, Alvin Alcorn, Manny Mineta.
What are these different guys specialize in?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: because Black Benny was a more street man parade man.

ctx.x: What kind of music did you have to play out there?

Well, we had to play practical all types. We had to play some slow numbers, some mediums, some fast, and some waltzes. I guess we'd play around, oh, eight, nine waltzes a night. We were more than that. Because every fourth of them, you had to play a waltz. You'd play a waltz, and you'd play a fast number, medium, or a slow drag, and then a waltz. That routine all night long, every fourth of them, you had to play a waltz. What hours you worked at? Oh, one hour. I mean, you go to work at eight, and you get off at…

Were you playing clarinet at this time of tour, or just all around to? Where? Well, around this time, did you pick up the clarinet once in a while, or all in a while? No. I mean, when you light the clarinet down, you more or less light it down. Forgot it. Yeah.
